description: Customer credentials in the Authorization header (identity-and-authz.md, "Telling the credentials apart"). A kit forwards `apiKey`, `oauth` and [being built] `ssoOauth` headers to org-api exactly as they came; everything else (kind null) is 401 unauthenticated without asking anyone, and never falls back to the cookie. A SCIM token (`ezgh_scim_` + 43 base62, `scimToken: true`) is no customer credential anywhere but the SCIM endpoint, which accepts nothing else (scim.md). Cases marked classifierOnly can't be reproduced over HTTP (the transport normalizes them): test them against the classifier only, never with a request. EZGH SSO resource tokens (`ezgh_sat_` + 43 base62) are forwarded; SSO refresh tokens (`ezgh_srt_`), client secrets (`ezgh_scs_`) and directory SCIM tokens (`ezgh_dsc_`) are refused on product routes. [being built] A project ingest key (`ezgh_ik_` + 43 base62, `ingestKey: true`) is refused on product routes, so its kind is null; an ingest host accepts it and `apiKey`, and nothing else (identity-and-authz.md, "Accepted on an ingest host"). [being built] Product data-plane keys (Feature Flags' SDK keys, `ezgh_fs_` and `ezgh_fc_` + 43 base62) are refused on product routes, so their kind is null; only their product's data host accepts them (identity-and-authz.md, "Product data-plane keys"). [being built] An observability client token (`ezgh_ct_` + 43 base62, `clientToken: true`) is never a header credential: its kind is null everywhere, and only a browser host's `ct` query parameter accepts it (identity-and-authz.md, "Observability client tokens"; vectors/browser-credentials.json).
